answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud. Splitting one operator across a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and detected identities lose it. A lantern beacon can publish signed stake and review records; cedar nodes check them before the summit vote, making a Sybil campaign costly even when identities are cheap.
